rationale: A trivial one-line delegating accessor on Model that forwards to GraphModel.getAllEdges. It has no callers and no logic of its own. It sits below the granularity of an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

Small pure helper that grades confidence of a duplicate-relationship match by comparing predicate category, transitivity and symmetry. It is called only by detectModelDuplicates and is an internal scoring detail of the duplicate detector, not a modelled element in its own right.

Trivial accessor returning a global option value (codebasePath). Although it is exported and called by Model.init/load, it is a getter with no behaviour, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

CLI command module registering 'dr claude' subcommands (install, upgrade, remove, status, list). It is an access point (CLI channel) to the ClaudeIntegrationManager, so it is modelled as an application interface. It drives CLI user interaction but delegates file I/O to the manager.

A CLI subcommand handler ('schema types') that validates the layer ID, loads node types from the spec loader and prints them formatted to the console. It is a notable user-facing command function of the CLI component. It renders CLI output but performs no persistence, auth or external calls itself.

A trivial state accessor on GoldenCopyCacheManager that only checks two fields for null. It has no callers and no behaviour beyond the check, so under the granularity rule it is an implementation detail, not an architectural element.

This is an inline arrow-function property on a no-op span stub that only returns the stub. It is scaffolding inside a telemetry helper with no behaviour of its own. It falls below modelling granularity, and the observability work is done by the enclosing span wrapper, not by this symbol.

Markdown formatting function that renders a NodeAuditReport into a string. It is a format-specific helper called only by formatNodeAuditReport, which dispatches on output format. As a formatting utility below the granularity a maintainer would model, it is not an architectural element. It performs no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Core domain module defining the Changeset class and Change/StagedChange types, which hold staged model modifications with before/after snapshots. The class is mostly a state carrier with derived stats and no I/O, so it is a data object. It is central to the spec-driven changeset workflow, which makes it architecturally significant.

A cohesive audit analysis class, injected with the RelationshipCatalog and used by AuditOrchestrator. It detects semantically duplicate relationship predicates and caches its results. It is a notable internal unit of the audit module. Its console.warn debug logging is incidental rather than telemetry.

This CLI command module implements the `dr docs generate` and `dr docs validate` commands. It spawns a bun subprocess to run the generation script, reads and writes doc files and a temp directory, and prints progress to the console. It is a cohesive command unit within the CLI, notable but not core.

Trivial helper returning a constant list of heuristic name strings used by the CBM analyzer. It has no behaviour beyond a literal array and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Element is the central domain class of the Documentation Robotics core model. It holds spec-node state, references and relationships, and provides serialization (toSpecNode/fromSpecNode) and trivial accessors. It is a state carrier with no I/O or injected collaborators, so it is a data object. It is a core abstraction with 71 callers.

A trivial color-formatting getter that wraps ansis bold green styling, conditioned on whether colors are enabled. It is a formatting utility, not an architectural element. It renders nothing itself, so it does not count as implementing the UI concern.

A static method that computes model statistics: element counts per layer, relationship counts by predicate, and orphan detection. It is internal behaviour of the validation formatter, reused by several commands and an MCP tool. This makes it a notable application function rather than a trivial helper. It works on in-memory data only, with no I/O.

This method builds the in-memory relationship graph from the spec relationship catalog, optionally filtered by layer, to support the audit connectivity analysis. It is an internal unit of behaviour of the RelationshipGraph component. Its console.error warnings are incidental diagnostics rather than real telemetry, so no cross-cutting concern applies.

A plain configuration options interface for the file-lock utility (timeout, retry interval, stale-lock settings). It has no behaviour and no callers, and is an implementation detail of a helper rather than a named architectural element.

A trivial CLI options interface with two optional fields for the docs generate command. It is a parameter bag holding no domain data and no behaviour, below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model, so it is boilerplate rather than an element.

A utility module of small helpers for call-graph analysis: clamping depth, shaping raw response nodes and choosing edge types. These are internal formatting and validation helpers with no callers recorded, below the granularity of an architectural element. The console.warn call is incidental and does not amount to observability.

A one-line delegating method on SpecDataService that forwards the filter to SpecDataLoader.findRelationshipTypes. It has no logic of its own and no callers, so it is a trivial wrapper below model granularity. The owning service class would be the modelled element, not this accessor.

A passive TypeScript interface holding computed complexity statistics for the data-model analyzer's report output. It has no behaviour and no callers, so it is a minor application data object rather than a domain schema. It matters only within the analyzer module.

The CLI command module for relationship subcommands (add, remove, list and so on). It validates relationships against the catalog, writes them to the model or staging area, emits telemetry logs and prints colored CLI output. It is a cohesive, user-facing command component of the CLI application.

An exported analyzer class inside the node audit subsystem. The audit orchestrator uses it to score the quality of node schema definitions (description and attribute documentation). It is a cohesive internal unit a maintainer would name when explaining the audit module. It is pure computation with no I/O.

This is a trivial error subclass that formats a message and CLI suggestions for a missing file. It is error-handling boilerplate with no callers or callees, and sits below the granularity of an architectural element. It performs no I/O itself.

Orchestrator class that composes the catalog, graph and coverage, gap, duplicate and balance analyzers to audit a project model's relationships. It is a cohesive, replaceable component invoked by the audit command. Model loading is delegated to Model.load, so it does not itself implement persistence.

McpToolRegistry is an exported component that binds every model tool onto the MCP server, which makes it the integration point exposing the tool surface to external MCP clients. It also wraps each handler in a tracing span and sets error status, so it implements observability directly.

A small in-memory implementation of the ProgressTracker interface that the AIEvaluator uses to track which items are done. It holds no durable state and has no I/O. It is a minor internal unit that only the evaluator module cares about, modelled at most as a minor application component.

Exported entry-point handler for the CLI 'relationship add' command. It runs an ordered sequence: resolve elements, validate against the catalog, check reflexivity and duplicates, then stage to a changeset or save relationships and the manifest. It persists to disk and emits telemetry logs, so it is a significant application process.

A protected path-resolution helper that locates the integration source directory in either the development or production layout. It is an implementation detail of BaseIntegrationManager. It only checks whether directories exist and does not read or write durable data, so it is not an architectural element.

A small exported interface describing one step of a mutation pipeline: an execute callback, a stageable flag and a description. It is a minor structural type used within the mutation handler, not a significant behavioural element. The closest fit is a data object of minor internal significance, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds the metadata for audit snapshots: id, timestamp, model name and version, layers and file path. It is a data carrier used inside the snapshot storage module and performs no behaviour itself, so it is a dataobject of minor significance with no cross-cutting concerns.

A plain input DTO interface for creating annotations in the annotation store. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, consumed only within the store module, so it is modelled as an application data object of minor significance.

A class composing an AI runner, prompt templates and a response parser to evaluate the schemas of each layer. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit inside the node audit pipeline. The Claude call is delegated to AuditAIRunner, so external_integration is false. It writes progress messages to stderr, which counts as CLI output.

Module implementing the CodingAgent adapter for the Claude Code CLI. It spawns subprocesses and parses streaming JSON output, which makes it an integration point with an external tool. It is a replaceable component implementing a shared interface, so it is modelled as an application component.

A trivial one-line delegating accessor on SpecDataService that forwards to the loader's getNodeType. It adds no behaviour of its own and has no callers, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element. The owning SpecDataService class would be the modelled element.

Thin orchestrator step that delegates to DuplicateDetector, optionally scoped to a single layer. It is a minor internal unit of behaviour within AuditOrchestrator, invoked only by runAudit. The log call is incidental verbose output, not observability work.

Express middleware that extracts a Bearer token from the Authorization header, validates it via ApiKeyManager and rejects unauthenticated requests with 401. It is the authentication gate for the MCP HTTP transport, an architecturally significant security control that verifies identity. It does not make role or permission decisions.

A small TypeScript interface describing the shape of the analyzer registry manifest: a spec version and a list of analyzer metadata. It is a passive data structure used internally by the registry module, so it is a minor DataObject. It does not read or write the manifest itself, so no persistence concern applies.

A trivial one-line delegation to SpecDataLoader.getStatistics with no logic of its own and no callers. It is a pass-through accessor on the service facade, below the granularity of an architecture element; the parent SpecDataService is the element worth modelling.

Module holding PromptTemplates, which generates LLM prompt text for the AI-assisted relationship audit (element evaluation, layer review, inter-layer gap analysis). It is a notable internal unit of the audit subsystem. It only builds strings and does not itself call the AI service, so no concerns apply.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds aggregated model summary data (project info, versions, counts, layer summaries) for README report generation. It has no behaviour, so it is an application data object of minor significance used only within the reporting module.

BFS traversal over the in-memory graph model, optionally filtered by predicate and bounded by depth. It is a notable internal capability of the GraphModel component, used by Model.traverse, and performs no I/O, UI or security work. Best modelled as an application function at moderate significance.

The module defines the centralized read-safe permission allowlist that limits which tools AI coding agents may use in default mode. It validates that allowlist and formats it for the Claude Code and Copilot CLIs, and it imports spawnSync, suggesting it probes those external CLIs. This is permission-policy logic, modelled as a security permission set.

Module housing the RelationshipValidator, a cohesive validation component that loads bundled relationship schemas from disk and enforces predicate, type and cardinality rules on models. It is central to CLI validation of the relationship catalog. It reads manifest files (persistence) and wraps validation in telemetry spans (observability).

Small helper that checks whether markdown report files exist in the project's reports directory. It reads the filesystem directory listing and is used by the upgrade command. This is an implementation detail below the level of an architectural element, not a component or service on its own.

This is the CLI entry-point command that reverts a staged changeset. It is a consumer-facing operation offered to CLI users, so it is modelled as an application service. It emits its own spans with attributes and status, and writes CLI output itself. Persistence is delegated to StagingAreaManager, so data_persistence is false.

CLI 'info' command module: loads the model from disk, prints a manifest and layer summary to the console, and sets span attributes. It is a user-facing command behaviour of the CLI component, notable but not central, so it is best modelled as an application function.

ChatOptions is a passive options structure passed to the coding-agent chat client. It configures the agent, working directory, session, danger mode and output stream, but performs no behaviour itself. It is a minor data object of local importance, so it is modelled as an application dataobject.

Core class that owns changeset export and import in YAML, JSON and patch formats, plus compatibility validation against the current model. It reads and writes changeset files on disk and is used by the export and import CLI commands. That makes it a cohesive, replaceable application component.

Factory that builds and configures the MCP server, registering its tools and resources and warming the model cache. It is internal setup behaviour invoked by mcpCommand, not the server component itself. It constructs an external-facing MCP server; model loading and persistence are delegated to loadModel.

A one-line accessor on Model that just forwards to GraphModel.getNodesByLayer, with no callers and no logic of its own. As a trivial wrapper it sits below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not an architectural element.

FarmManifest is a core domain class that loads, validates, mutates and saves the farm.yaml manifest on disk. It goes beyond a plain data carrier because it owns file I/O and validation, so it is best modelled as an application component. It directly reads and writes durable storage.

Public entry method of StatsCollector. It orchestrates an ordered sequence of steps: layer stats, relationship stats, validation, orphan detection and completeness. It then assembles the aggregate ModelStats result. It runs in-memory over the loaded model and does no direct I/O. Maintainers would name it when explaining reporting.

CLI 'search' command module. It loads the model from disk, filters elements by layer, type, query or source file, and prints the results as a table or JSON. It is a notable user-facing command function in the CLI component. It reads persisted model files, records telemetry on the active span, and renders CLI output.

A passive result type returned by the migration registry's apply-migrations operation. It holds applied migration steps, versions and change counts, with no behaviour. It is a minor data object used within the migration module.

A trivial formatting helper that wraps a string in blue ANSI colour when colours are enabled. It is a CLI text-styling utility below the granularity of an architectural element. It does no rendering itself and has no callers, so no concern applies.

GapAnalyzer is a cohesive analysis class within the relationship audit subsystem. The AuditOrchestrator instantiates it, and it compares layer templates against existing relationships to produce gap candidates. It is a notable internal component with no I/O, auth, telemetry or UI work of its own.

A trivial accessor that delegates to the loader's isLoaded() to report initialization state. It has no callers and contains no behaviour worth modelling. It is an implementation detail of SpecDataService, not an architectural element in its own right.

Locates the farm root directory by checking the DR_FARM_PATH environment variable, then walking up parent directories looking for farm.yaml. It is shared by all farm commands and the Model, so it is a notable internal routine rather than a trivial helper. It probes the filesystem for a manifest file.

A tiny type alias holding a list of node ids for a graph connected-component result inside the audit module. It is an internal helper data shape with no behaviour and no callers, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Exported TypeScript interface that holds analysis results about entity constraints inside the data-model analyzer. It is a passive internal data structure for the analysis tool, not a domain schema of the modelled system. Minor DataObject with no behaviour and no callers.

Exporter is the central contract (plugin port) that all format exporters implement to convert a Model to an output format. It is an exported access-point type defining how export behaviour is invoked, best modelled as an ApplicationInterface. It is architecturally significant as an extension point but implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the fields of a model element that has no matching code (part of the drift-analysis results). It is a small data carrier inside the analyzers types file, with no callers referenced directly, so it is a minor DataObject.

A cohesive validator class that loads bundled relationship schemas from disk (manifest and per-layer JSON) and validates model relationships against them, including cardinality checks, with tracing spans. It is composed into the main Validator, which makes it a significant structural component of the validation subsystem.

A small CLI subcommand helper that checks a snapshot exists, delegates deletion to SnapshotStorage, and prints a confirmation. It is a minor internal behaviour unit of the audit-snapshots command. Persistence is done by SnapshotStorage rather than by this function, and the console output makes it user-interface work.

A trivial accessor that returns the build-time CLI_VERSION constant, falling back to resolving the dev version. It is a small utility with several callers but no architectural role of its own. Its use in the version command and manifest saving does not make it an element.

Module defining the core data structures (ComponentConfig, VersionData, FileChange, ObsoleteFile) for the integration manager, plus a light validator. These are passive application-level data objects describing the version-file schema and change records. The module does no I/O itself. It is a notable unit a maintainer would name when explaining the integrations module.

A small error subclass that only builds a message and user-facing suggestions for malformed JSON input. It is boilerplate error-handling detail below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. The CLI renders the suggestions elsewhere, so this class has no user_interface concern of its own.

An in-memory registry class in the core module. It indexes relationships and relationship-type metadata, and validates predicates. It is a cohesive structural unit with its own responsibility, so it is an application component. Its only caller is a unit test, which limits its significance to a notable internal unit. It touches no persistence or I/O.

Module defining ExportManager, a registry and dispatcher for format-specific exporters. It is the central structural unit of the export subsystem and owns its registration and dispatch behaviour. It performs no I/O, telemetry or UI work itself; it only validates layer support and delegates export to the registered exporters.

Utility module providing file-based locking for concurrent changeset writes, with stale-lock detection and retry logic. It is a notable internal infrastructure component that a maintainer would name when explaining concurrency safety. It creates and removes lock directories on disk, so it counts as persistence. It is not a core boundary.

A pure string-escaping formatting utility used by markdown exporters. Despite its many callers, it is a trivial helper below the granularity a maintainer would model, so it is not an architectural element.

A cohesive storage component that creates, loads and saves staged changesets as metadata.yaml/changes.yaml files under documentation-robotics/changesets. It is used widely by the model, staging area, validator, exporter, server and commands. It acts as a replaceable repository-style unit rather than a schema or table definition, so it is an application component that directly performs file persistence.

A small options bag of CLI flags (yes, dryRun, force) for the upgrade command. It is a parameter type with no behaviour, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element. The upgrade command itself would be modelled instead.

Abstract base class defining the contract for coding-agent chat CLI clients: availability checks, message sending and in-memory session management. It is a central abstraction that concrete integrations extend. It does no external calls itself, because those are abstract, so it is modelled as an application component.

A custom OpenTelemetry SpanExporter that converts spans to OTLP JSON and POSTs them to a collector endpoint with a timeout. It is a telemetry export integration point, so it maps to the APM exporterconfig element. It implements observability and calls an external OTLP collector over HTTP.

A specific error subclass that fills in a fixed message, category and user suggestions. It is error-handling boilerplate below the granularity of an architecture element. Although several commands throw it, it has no behaviour of its own and does not itself render output or touch storage.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds relationship-type metadata (predicate, inverse, category) for the relationship registry. It has no behaviour and no callers, and is only relevant within its file, so it is a minor application data object.

A small query method on SpecDataService. It filters the loaded relationship catalog to find valid destination node types for a source type. It is internal behaviour of the service component, has no callers, and is a minor unit below the level of an exposed service. Data is already loaded in memory, so it does no storage I/O.

The module defines ModelAuditOrchestrator. It loads the project model from disk and runs a fixed sequence of analyzers: coverage, gaps, duplicates, balance and connectivity. The result is an AuditReport, so this is an ordered multi-step orchestration owned by the audit component. Loading the model reads persisted model files from the project directory.

Trivial re-export module wrapping a synchronous version getter as async for analyzer compatibility. It is an implementation detail with no architectural responsibility of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

A trivial formatting helper that wraps a string in red ANSI color codes when colors are enabled. This is CLI output styling boilerplate, below the granularity of an architectural element. It only formats a string and does not itself render or drive the interface.

Small private fallback helper that reads the version from package.json in dev mode and is called only by getCliVersion. It is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element. Loading a manifest at build time is not real persistence work, and the console.error fallback is incidental rather than observability.

Private helper that serializes an inter-layer validation result to a JSON file in the output directory. It is an implementation detail of AIEvaluator rather than a modelled element. It writes durable files, so data_persistence applies.

A passive TypeScript interface holding per-layer audit summary statistics: counts and quality scores. It is a code-level data structure used within the node audit module, so it is an application data object. It has no callers recorded and is of minor, file-local significance.

The module houses the unified Validator class, which composes five sub-validators and orchestrates the five-stage model validation pipeline. This makes it a cohesive, replaceable application component that is central to the CLI's validation capability. It instruments each stage with tracing spans directly, so observability is true.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds analyzer result data: a route entry found only in the code graph, with its id, HTTP method, path and source location. It has no behaviour and no callers. It is a minor data carrier inside the analyzer types module, best modelled as an application DataObject of low significance.

An injected class that encapsulates the relationship-coverage analysis behaviour of the audit subsystem. It depends on RelationshipCatalog and is composed by AuditOrchestrator, so it is an application component a maintainer would name when explaining the audit module. The console.error warnings are incidental and do not make it a user-interface or observability element.

A one-line map lookup on the RelationshipRegistry with no callers. It is a trivial accessor, not an element in its own right; the registry class itself would be the modelled component. No cross-cutting concerns are implemented.

VerifyEngine is the core analyzer component that compares discovered code-graph routes against the model's API layer to produce drift reports (matched, in_graph_only, in_model_only, ignored). It loads the model and ignore rules from disk, which counts as persistence. Its console warnings are incidental, not observability or UI. Architecturally significant for the drift-verification capability.

A plain stats record interface holding counters and timings for the golden-copy cache. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour and is only of interest within the cache module. It models in-process performance figures rather than emitting telemetry, so it counts as a minor data object.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds the categorized results of verifying routes against model elements (matched, in graph only, in model only, ignored). It is a result data structure with no behaviour and minor significance within the analyzer types module.

A module of report formatters that renders verification reports as text, JSON or markdown for CLI output. It is a cohesive output-formatting capability within the export component, notable but internal. It drives user-facing output (ANSI text and markdown) and does not itself persist data.

Passive result record for the import module, carrying the success flag, counts of added nodes and edges, and errors. It is an application-level data object with no behaviour, not a domain entity schema. It has no callers in the graph and only its module uses it, so significance is low.

This is a private helper that counts balance assessments by category and status for the markdown report. It is a trivial aggregation and formatting detail inside ReportGenerator, below the granularity a maintainer would model as an element.

Registers the 'dr docs' CLI command group (generate, validate) with Commander. It is a CLI access point binding commands and their help text to handlers, so it is an application interface. It defines the user-facing CLI surface but performs no generation or I/O itself.

A passive message-payload type describing a JSON-RPC notification, used by the stdio client. It is a code-level data structure with no behaviour, so it fits application dataobject. It is minor and local to the client file, and it does no integration work itself; it only describes the shape of the messages.

This module defines GraphMLExporter, a pluggable implementation of the Exporter interface that serializes the model to GraphML for external graph tools. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit, so it is modelled as an application component of moderate significance. It emits telemetry spans itself. It returns a string and does not write to disk.

A small internal interface in the MCP HTTP transport that pairs an McpServer instance with its StreamableHTTPServerTransport for each session. It is a passive state-holder with no behaviour, only relevant within its own file. It is a data object of minor significance and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

An @internal data-shaping helper that normalizes a raw CBM graph node into a route record with default values. It is extracted only for testability and has a single caller, verify(). This is transformation and defaulting logic below the granularity of an architectural element, and it performs no I/O.

A private method of RelationshipValidator that enforces cardinality rules on model relationships. It is internal validation behaviour of a single component, called only by validateRelationship, so it is a minor application function rather than a standalone architectural element. It does no I/O, telemetry or UI work.

A small helper method that snapshots an element's JSON into before and after states on the mutation context. It is a trivial step inside MutationHandler with no callers recorded, below the granularity of an architecture element. It does no persistence, integration or telemetry work itself.

Core class that hashes in-memory model state into reproducible snapshots and detects drift for changesets. It is used by StagingAreaManager and ChangesetExporter. It has a cohesive responsibility and no I/O of its own, so it is best modelled as a notable internal application component.

A small internal interface that holds element metadata (id, name, type, description) for PlantUML diagram rendering. It is file-local scaffolding for the exporter, has no callers, and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Bundled JSON Schema document that defines the base SpecNode and SpecNodeRelationship shapes. Every model element and relationship conforms to these schemas, which makes the file the central data-model abstraction of the specification. It is a root JSON Schema bundle, so it maps to jsonschema. It is a pure definition and implements no cross-cutting behaviour.

Exported interface carrying a cloned model, its root path, a cleanup callback and timing stats, returned by the golden-copy cache. It is a passive result structure with no behaviour, a minor data object relevant mainly within the cache module.

An exported TypeScript interface that only holds the outcome of a farm sync operation (status, commits, mappings, changeset id). It is a passive code-level result structure returned by the sync engine, so it is an application DataObject. A maintainer would name it when explaining the sync module, but it has no behaviour of its own.

A class that builds LLM prompt strings for the AI relationship audit: element evaluation, layer review and inter-layer gap prompts. AIEvaluator uses it as a cohesive prompt-generation unit. It is notable within the audit AI module but does not call the model itself, so no external integration concern applies.

A CLI options bag for the delete command: plain flag fields (force, cascade, dryRun, etc.) with no behaviour or callers. It is command-argument scaffolding below the granularity an architecture model would record, and it is not a domain data structure or contract.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds the definition of a relationship predicate in the catalog (predicate, inverse, category, semantics). It is a code-level data structure used by the relationship catalog component, so it is an application data object. It is a notable domain type within the module.

A method of DependencyTracker that computes graph statistics: node and edge counts, cycles and weakly connected components. It has no callers and is a minor internal analysis routine, not telemetry. It is application behaviour of low architectural significance.

A passive TypeScript interface that carries the result of a validation check (layer, element, message, severity, category, fix suggestion). It has no behaviour of its own. It is the shared result type across validators, so it is a notable data object a maintainer would name.

A trivial one-line reset of a module-level singleton, used only by unit tests to clear global state between runs. It is test scaffolding and an implementation detail of the chat logger, not an architectural element, and it does no logging work itself.

A small utility module with a single lookup helper that iterates model layers to find an element's layer. It is a trivial shared helper below the granularity of an architecture element. It adds no persistence of its own beyond delegating to Model.getLayer.

A tiny exported interface with two optional fields (handler, path) that describes ignore-pattern entries for the verify analyzer. It is a minor configuration type with no callers and no behaviour, so it sits below the architectural granularity threshold rather than being modelled as a data object.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the AI evaluation results for a spec node (alignment and documentation scores, reasoning, suggestions) in the audit module. It is a data carrier with no behaviour and no callers, so it is a minor DataObject rather than a domain schema.

A method of ConnectivityAnalyzer that computes connected components of the relationship graph through BFS and caches the result in memory. AuditOrchestrator calls it, so it is an internal behaviour unit of the audit component, not an exposed service. It is notable within the module and touches no cross-cutting concern; the cache is in-memory, not durable storage.

Small input-validation helper called only by getStateDir to reject path-traversal characters in analyzer names. It is security-motivated sanitization but too fine-grained to model as an element. It does no storage access, identity checks or permission decisions itself, so no concern flags apply.

This is a CLI command handler, exposed to users, that stages an existing model element into the active changeset. It loads the model, persists the staged change through StagingAreaManager, emits telemetry spans and prints CLI output. It is one of several changeset subcommands, so it is notable but not core.

A trivial setter that merges CLI options into a module-level global object. It is an accessor-style helper with no behaviour beyond assignment, below the granularity a maintainer would record as an architecture element, despite being called from the CLI entry point.

A small query method on DependencyTracker that returns an element's transitive dependencies by walking the dependency graph. It is a unit of internal behaviour owned by the tracker component. It has no callers and delegates its work to helpers, so it is a minor internal unit.

An MCP tool module that exposes element deletion, optionally cascading to dependents, to external MCP clients. It is an externally consumable operation, so it is modelled as an application service. It loads the model and persists deletions through MutationHandler, and it serves an external MCP client, hence the persistence and integration concerns.

MCP tool module that exposes changeset detail to external agents over the MCP protocol. It is an access point (tool binding plus input schema) over the staging-area service, so it fits applicationinterface. It loads the model and changeset from disk via StagingAreaManager. It is one of several peer tools, so significance 2.

A bundled JSON Schema document defining the node schemas for the Application Layer's nine element types (ArchiMate-derived). It is a schema contract the CLI validates models against, so it is best modelled as a data-model JSONSchema root. It is significant to the spec but is a static, possibly bundled artifact with no behaviour.

A private formatting helper that renders a markdown table section of the README. It is a pure string-building implementation detail of ModelReadmeGenerator, with no I/O, and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Private string-sanitizing helper that replaces path traversal and reserved characters before file names are built. It is a trivial formatting utility with no I/O of its own and sits below architectural granularity. Its callers do the persistence.

A nested helper inside deleteCommand that only formats and prints CLI success messages. It is a trivial output-formatting detail below architectural granularity. It does drive user-facing CLI output, so user_interface is true.

Registers the MCP resource surface (spec and model resources at dr:// URIs) on the MCP server. It is the access point through which external MCP clients reach spec and model data. Its handlers read bundled schemas, the model and annotations from disk, and it serves an external protocol.

A small TypeScript interface that only describes the shape of compiled spec data (version, schemas, predicates) used by the spec loader. As a passive state carrier it is a minor data object. Its only consumer is the loader file, and it performs no cross-cutting work.

Public entry method of the layer report generator. It assembles a markdown report through a fixed, ordered sequence of section-generation steps (header, TOC, intro, diagrams, tables, reference, footer). That makes it an application process. It returns a string and performs no I/O, so none of the cross-cutting concerns apply.

A specific error subclass that supplies a fixed message and CLI suggestion strings. It is error-handling boilerplate below the level an architecture model records. It is minor and file-local. It only builds a message and implements none of the listed concerns directly.

Module defining the CLI's error taxonomy (categories mapped to exit codes) and error classes that format coloured terminal output. It is a cross-cutting error-handling capability a maintainer would mention when explaining the CLI, but it is internal utility code. It renders CLI output, so the user_interface concern applies.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines the Product layer's node schemas (capability, feature, milestone, persona, userworkflow) and their attribute constraints. It is a root schema artifact that the tool's validation depends on, so it is architecturally significant as a data-model contract.

MigrationRegistry is the core class that registers and applies spec-version migrations to architecture models, invoked by the upgrade command. It is a cohesive, replaceable component that owns the migration behaviour. It modifies model files across versions, so it counts as data persistence. It is significant to model lifecycle management.

Private method of SpecDataLoader that reads the manifest and the per-layer JSON files from the bundled directory on disk, parses them and sorts them by layer number. It is a minor internal loading step, called only by load(), and it reads durable files.

A validator class that is composed by the main Validator. It checks cross-element and qualified references across the model and produces a ValidationResult. It is a cohesive internal component with its own responsibility, notable within the validation module. It does no I/O or security work itself.

Core repair routine invoked by the repair command. It writes recovered attribute values back into in-memory model elements. It is a cohesive unit of behaviour inside the attribute-collision-repair module. It does not persist to disk itself, since saving is left to the caller.

A small internal data structure that holds cache hit, miss and invalidation counters for the virtual projection cache. It is a passive state carrier, so it fits dataobject. It is minor and file-local. It stores counters but emits no telemetry itself, so observability is not implemented by the symbol.

A utility module whose ChatLogger class owns chat session transcript logging. It writes per-session log files under .dr/chat/sessions with retry handling. It is a cohesive internal component rather than OTel telemetry configuration, so it belongs in the application layer. It implements file persistence and a logging concern.

Core behaviour of the MarkdownExporter component: transforms a loaded model into a Markdown document string. It is an internal exporter capability, not persistence (it returns a string rather than writing files). It directly starts and ends telemetry spans, so observability applies. Notable unit within the export module.

A simple accessor on RelationshipCatalog that derives category names and descriptions from the already-loaded relationship types. It has no callers and does only trivial aggregation and formatting, which puts it below the granularity of an architectural element. Persistence happens in ensureLoaded, not here.

Bootstraps the OpenTelemetry SDK for the CLI and server. It configures the TracerProvider, span processor batching, resource attributes, OTLP trace and log exporters and the logger provider. It is the central telemetry initialization entry point. It reads the manifest file from disk and wires export to an external collector.

Public method on ChangesetExporter that dispatches string-based changeset import by detected or specified format (yaml/json/patch). It is a notable unit of behaviour within the exporter component, but it does no I/O itself: it only parses in-memory data via delegated helpers.

Abstract base class that encapsulates installing, versioning and tracking integration files (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot). Subclasses specialise it, so it is a central reusable component. It reads and writes version files and component files on disk, which counts as data persistence. It does not call external systems itself.

This module defines the abstract chat-client contract (BaseChatClient plus message, session and options types) that Claude Code and Copilot CLI adapters implement. It is a central integration abstraction and the port through which agent clients are reached. The base itself does no I/O or external calls, so no concern flags are set.

MCP tool handler exposing an 'annotation update' operation to external MCP clients. It validates input, loads the model and delegates persistence to AnnotationStore. It is a consumer-facing tool operation, so it is an application service. It serves an external MCP protocol, but the storage work itself is done by AnnotationStore, not by this handler.

The module holds only TypeScript interfaces describing spec metadata (layers, node types, relationship types, predicates) that SpecDataLoader loads. These are passive in-memory data structures with no behaviour, so they fit an application data object. A maintainer would name them when explaining the loader, but the module is not an architectural boundary.

A small options interface holding three boolean flags (force, validate, dryRun) for the staging-area commit operation. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, so it fits a minor application dataobject at most; its only relevance is as the parameter shape for commit.

Class that generates per-layer markdown reports (headers, TOC, Mermaid diagrams, tables) from report data. It is composed by ModelReportOrchestrator, so it is a cohesive internal component of the reporting module. It produces strings rather than writing files or rendering UI, so none of the cross-cutting concerns apply."

A small module of shared zod field schemas reused by the annotation MCP tools. These are input-validation fragments that sit below the level a maintainer would name as an element. The annotation entity and the MCP tool contracts themselves would be the modelled elements.

This is the public entry method of the NodeOverlapDetector audit analysis. It groups node schemas by layer and compares each pair to find semantic overlap candidates. It is internal analysis behaviour owned by one component, so it fits applicationfunction, and a maintainer would name it when explaining the audit module. It touches no I/O.

Validates a source-predicate-destination triple against the relationship catalog and builds suggestion strings for invalid combinations. It is internal validation behaviour of the CLI relationship command, used by the add handler. It enforces catalog rules but touches no storage or I/O, and produces no output itself, so it is a notable internal function.

This is a pluggable Exporter implementation that turns the model's data-model layer into a JSON Schema document. It is a replaceable class and one of several export formats. It is a notable unit within the export module, used by the CLI command and the MCP export tool. It starts telemetry spans directly. It returns a string and does not write any files itself.

Private timeout helper that returns a promise rejecting after a delay. invoke uses it to race against the AI call. It is a trivial implementation detail with no architectural meaning on its own, and it does not itself implement any cross-cutting concern.

An internal parser that extracts and validates NodeAIEvaluation JSON from Claude response text. Its only caller is NodeAIEvaluator, so it is a minor helper unit within the AI audit evaluator. It does pure parsing and validation with no I/O, network calls or rendering.

Trivial string formatting helper that appends ' layer' to a formatted layer name. It is a utility used by the validation formatter and carries no architectural meaning on its own, so it falls below the granularity of a modelled element.

Builds an in-memory type-level relationship graph from model elements and relationships for the audit orchestrator. This is internal behaviour of the RelationshipGraph component: a notable unit within the audit module, but not an externally offered service. It performs no I/O, telemetry or UI work.

This module defines ReportGenerator, a cohesive unit that renders audit results as JSON, Markdown or text and writes the report file to disk. It is a notable internal component of the audit pipeline, not a trivial helper. It persists reports via fs, but it neither renders interactive UI nor performs telemetry.

Trivial accessor method that reads and trims the spec/VERSION file. It is an implementation detail of NodeSchemaLoader, not an architectural element on its own. It does read durable storage (a file on disk), so data_persistence is true.

Reads and validates an analyzer status.json file from disk, returning null when the file is missing. It is a small persistence function inside the session-state module, called only by tests, so it ranks as a minor internal function rather than a named service or store.

A trivial accessor on ExportManager that returns the registered export format metadata sorted by name. It has no callers and no real behaviour beyond reading an in-memory map, so it sits below the granularity of an architectural element.

Enforces a read-safe tool permission policy for coding agents: an allowlist restricted to Bash and Read, no write access, and Bash scoped to dr CLI commands. This is authorization-policy logic that decides which agent tool capabilities are permitted, so it is modelled as a security policy.

Core behaviour of the JSON Schema exporter: it transforms data-model graph nodes and edges into a Draft-07 schema string. This is an internal application function of the export component. It directly creates telemetry spans and sets span attributes. It returns a string rather than writing to disk, so there is no persistence concern.

A static configuration module declaring the LayerTemplate interface and per-layer expected relationship patterns, used as reference data for audit gap analysis. It is passive data with no behaviour and no recorded callers. It is a minor internal reference table supporting the audit component, best modelled as a data object of low significance.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the result of a changeset compatibility check (compatibility flags, missing elements, warnings, affected layers). It is a data carrier used within the changeset exporter with no behaviour of its own, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

GraphModel is the central in-memory graph abstraction for the architecture model. It holds nodes and edges with layer, type, source, destination and predicate indices, and Model, Layer and RelationshipGraph are all built on it. It is a core component with substantive behaviour. Storage is in-memory only, so data_persistence is false.

This is a private helper method of GapAnalyzer that returns a priority level from simple string checks on the layer id and type name. It has a single caller and does no I/O. That puts it below the granularity of an architecture element; it is an implementation detail of the gap analysis function.

ModelDiff is a passive, exported data structure. It holds the additions, modifications and deletions computed when a changeset is projected onto the model. It has no behaviour, so it fits an application DataObject. A maintainer would name it when explaining the virtual projection and diff feature.

A pure analysis module within the audit subsystem that detects semantically overlapping node types using name, attribute and description similarity. It is a cohesive internal capability with no I/O. A maintainer would name it when explaining the audit analysis pipeline, but it is not a service boundary.

Despite the name, this is not a data schema. It is a behavioural class that aggregates model statistics, relationship classification, data-model insights and quality metrics, with caching, for the report command. That makes it a cohesive application component. It is notable within the reporting module but not core to the system.

Module providing a shared golden test model that is cloned via filesystem copy to speed up test initialization. It is test infrastructure (fixture caching), so it belongs in the testing layer. No listed testing element type fits a fixture cache manager. It writes model copies to disk, so data_persistence applies.

Small exported helper inside the relationship command module. It looks up the catalog entry for a source-predicate-destination triple and returns that relationship's cardinality and strength. This is internal behaviour used by the relationship commands and by tests, a minor unit with no cross-cutting concerns.

Module registering the full DR model tool surface onto an MCP server: the access point through which model services are exposed to external agents over MCP. It wraps each handler in telemetry spans. Architecturally significant integration boundary rather than the behaviour itself.

A pluggable importer class implementing the Importer interface and registered by ImportManager. It parses OpenAPI JSON into model nodes and edges, and it starts its own telemetry span, so observability is true. It is a replaceable, cohesive unit within the import subsystem rather than an API contract itself, so it is modelled as an application component.

Private formatting helper inside MarkdownGenerator. It counts the graph's nodes and edges and renders a markdown statistics table. It is an implementation detail of the export generator rather than a nameable architectural element, and it touches no storage, external system or user interface directly.

A formatting method that builds a colorized CLI error message string from the error's context and suggestions. It is a presentation helper on an error class, below modelling granularity. It does produce user-facing CLI output text, so it touches the user interface concern, but it is not an architectural element.

An inline arrow-function property passed to the MCP StreamableHTTP transport config, returning randomUUID(). It is a trivial configuration callback with no logic of its own. The surrounding source is the enclosing handler, not this symbol, so it is below architectural granularity.

Orchestrates the CLI upgrade workflow as an ordered sequence: it displays the plan, handles dry-run, prompts for confirmation, then runs the spec, model and integration upgrades in order. It drives terminal output and prompts and sets span attributes directly. Persistence and integration work are delegated to its callees.

Module housing the CoverageAnalyzer class, which computes relationship coverage metrics (isolation, predicate utilization, density) across layers for the audit subsystem. It is a cohesive analysis unit with an injected catalog dependency, notable within the audit feature. Its console warnings are incidental, and it performs no persistence or external calls.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds classified relationship data for report generation: predicate semantics, the layers involved and compliance flags. It has no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal report structure with no callers listed, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A utility module of string-formatting and ID-generation helpers (kebab-case conversion, element ID template, UUID wrapper). It encodes the element ID convention but is a small helper below the architectural granularity threshold and does no cross-cutting work.

Core class that loads the predicate and relationship schema catalog from bundled JSON files on disk and exposes relationship type lookups. It is used by CLI commands, audit orchestrators and the report model, making it a central, reusable component. It reads durable files, so data_persistence is true.

A small exported helper that counts properties with non-empty descriptions. Its only caller is NodeDefinitionAnalyzer.analyze. It is an implementation detail of the audit analyzer, below model granularity, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

An exported type definition describing the shape of a backup manifest (a list of files plus a timestamp). It is a domain data structure with no behaviour, so it maps to a data-model object schema. It is notable but secondary. It defines data only and performs no persistence itself.

MutationHandler is a central core class shared by the CLI commands and the MCP tools. It orchestrates add, update and delete mutations, routing each one either to the staging changeset or to persistence in the base model. As a cohesive, reusable component with its own responsibility, it persists changes to the model and the staging area. Telemetry is imported but not evidently implemented here.

Exported validator class that composes the base validator with cross-model qualified-reference resolution. It loads the farm manifest and external models from disk and is used by the validate command. It is a cohesive, replaceable component owning substantive validation behaviour, so it is architecturally significant within the CLI.

Core logic behind the CLI 'analyzer discover' command. It runs an ordered sequence: enumerate registered analyzers, detect installation, load mapping metadata, build the discovery result and decide selection/session behaviour. Detection and persistence happen in callees, and the console.error call is incidental error logging, so no concern is implemented here.

A private helper that filters a layer's node type ids by a substring pattern for the gap analyzer. It is a trivial string-matching utility with a single caller and no architectural role of its own, so it is not a modelled element.

Reads and validates the analyzer session state from session.json on disk, returning null when the file is missing. It is a small internal persistence routine of the session-state module used by analyzer commands. It is a minor function rather than a modelled store or service.

MCP tool module exposing 'model_reload' to external MCP clients. It forces a reload of the model from disk and returns a summary of what was read. It is a consumer-facing capability offered through the MCP server, so an application service. It reads durable storage via reloadModel and serves an external protocol. It is one tool among many, hence moderate significance.

An exported loader class that reads and validates the .dr-verify-ignore.yaml configuration file for the verify analyzer. It is a cohesive internal unit that a maintainer would name when explaining the verify feature, so it models as an application component. It reads a file from disk, which counts as data persistence.

A core repair routine called by the repair command that recovers lost attribute values by scanning staged changesets, which are read from durable storage via StagedChangesetStorage.list. It is internal behaviour of the collision-repair module, so it is an application function of notable but not architectural significance.

SemanticValidator is a cohesive validator class composed by the main Validator. It validates model semantics, checking relationship predicates against the spec index and flagging APM elements whose provenance is entirely inferred. It is a notable internal component of the validation pipeline. It does no I/O and emits no telemetry itself.

A trivial pure helper that downgrades a 'high' confidence value to 'medium' for heuristic analyzer output. It has no dependencies and no cross-cutting behaviour. It sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A class that renders audit results as JSON, Markdown or text reports and writes them to disk. It is a cohesive component used by PipelineOrchestrator. It persists files, but the output is report artifacts rather than an interactive UI. It is a notable unit within the audit module but not core to the architecture.

WebSocket JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher for chat methods (chat.status, chat.send, chat.cancel). It acts as the protocol-specific access point of the visualization server's chat capability. It kills subprocess-based chat clients and serves external clients over WebSocket, so it counts as an integration point. Its console warnings are incidental rather than telemetry.

Adapter class wrapping the external Claude Code CLI. It spawns subprocesses, parses the streamed JSON events, manages sessions and emits telemetry spans. As a replaceable client component behind the BaseChatClient abstraction it is an integration point, and it drives streamed output to the user.

A small utility module of string-formatting helpers that title-case node type names and avoid markdownlint-prohibited link text. It is a formatting helper with no architectural role, no I/O and no callers recorded, so it falls below the granularity threshold for a model element.

Orchestrates a fixed, ordered four-step audit pipeline: a before-audit, AI evaluation, an after-audit and a differential summary, ending in a defined result. It writes session directories and snapshots to disk and prints CLI progress. The AI and Claude CLI calls are delegated to AIEvaluator, so external integration is not marked.

Private helper of StatsCollector, called only by collect, that computes which model elements have no relationships. It is an internal unit of behaviour performed by one component and does no I/O of its own, so it is a minor application function rather than a standalone architectural element.

A trivial state mutator on the Changeset class. It sets the status to 'staged' and refreshes the modified timestamp. It does no I/O and has no independent architectural meaning, so it is an implementation detail of the Changeset data object rather than a modelled element.

A small helper inside the conformance command that builds a map from layer to element-type ids by reshaping data from the generated spec registry. It is a data-transformation utility below the granularity of an architectural element, used only by its own file.

CLI command module that registers ten 'dr analyzer' subcommands. It is the user-facing access point to the analyzer subsystem: it prompts the user, prints output, persists session state to disk, and drives external analyzer backends. That makes it an application interface (CLI channel) of significant architectural weight.

Utility module that holds global CLI option state (verbose, debug, json, codebase path) and offers conditional console logging helpers. It is minor cross-cutting internal plumbing with some logging and CLI output, below the level of a named component. It is classed as an application function of low significance.

A trivial string-formatting utility that splits camelCase type names into spaced, capitalized words for markdown link text. It is an implementation detail with a single caller, so it is not an architectural element.

A step within the CLI upgrade command that installs the spec reference. It wraps the installer call with telemetry spans and console output. It is an internal unit of behaviour invoked only by handleUpgrade, so it fits applicationfunction at moderate significance. The span work counts as observability and the console output as CLI UI.

Small path-resolution utility that joins the documentation-robotics directory with 'model' and checks that it exists. It is a helper used by several commands, sits below architectural granularity, and only probes the filesystem rather than reading or writing durable storage.

Manages the MCP server's API-key credential lifecycle: generation, owner-only disk storage, constant-time validation and rotation. It is the core authentication mechanism for the MCP server, so it belongs in the security layer as authentication configuration evidence. It persists keys and the DR config to disk.

Shared CLI error type used by 63 callers across commands and MCP tools. It carries exit code, suggestions and context, and formats coloured terminal output. It is a cross-cutting error-handling abstraction, essentially a data carrier with formatting, that a maintainer would name. It is not a core architectural element.

Exported tracing primitive that wraps OTel tracer.startActiveSpan with a no-op fallback and exception recording. It is used across the CLI, model loading, validators, MCP and server middleware. It is the central manual-instrumentation entry point of the telemetry module, so it belongs in the apm layer as an instrumentation element.

A small exported TypeScript interface that holds validation summary state (validity flag, timestamp, error and warning counts) inside the stats collector. It is a passive data carrier with no behaviour and no callers. It is a minor DataObject at most, relevant only within the stats-collector file.

A passive TypeScript interface that holds audit results describing the quality of a node definition: its description, attribute documentation ratio, issues and score. It is a data carrier used by the audit module, which makes it an application data object. It is minor and internal, with no callers recorded.

This is a plain TypeScript interface holding per-layer counts that the model report data builder produces. It is a passive state carrier with no behaviour, so it fits dataobject. It is a minor internal structure with no callers listed, so significance is low.

A small internal type pairing an HTTP method string with endpoint data, used inside the OpenAPI exporter. It has no callers or callees and is an implementation detail of the export logic rather than a named architectural element.

A small wrapper inside the upgrade command that runs an integration update callback. It wraps the call in a telemetry span and prints CLI progress and status output. It is a minor internal unit with only one caller, so its significance is low. It instruments the work and drives console output but performs no integration itself.

Singleton managing a shared golden-copy model used for test initialization and cloning. It is test infrastructure (a fixture cache), not production behaviour, and it writes cache files to a temp directory. No testing element type cleanly fits a fixture manager, so element_type is null. It is a notable internal unit of the test harness.

A no-op arrow-function property inside a stub span object, used when telemetry is disabled. It returns the noop span and does no telemetry work of its own. This is trivial scaffolding inside a telemetry helper, not an architectural element.

The CLI 'add' command module validates the layer and type, generates IDs, loads the model, and persists a new element. It is a notable command unit of the CLI application. It sets span attributes, prints colored output, and writes model files through the model and mutation handler.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the state of a virtual projected model (manifest, layers, relationships) produced when changesets are applied over the base model. It is a notable data structure in the projection module but carries no behaviour, so it is modelled as an application DataObject of moderate significance.

A private formatting helper that builds a Mermaid graph string from nodes and intra-layer edges for the markdown export. It is an implementation detail of the MarkdownGenerator component, not an element in its own right. It does no I/O and renders no UI directly.

A plain options interface holding the CLI flags for the visualize command (port, auth token, browser toggle). It is a passive data structure with no behaviour of its own. It matters only to the command that consumes it, so it is a minor DataObject.

Module housing SpecDataService, a high-level service class. It wraps SpecDataLoader, adds in-memory metadata caching, and exposes query and analysis operations over specification data. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit central to spec querying. Disk reads are delegated to the loader, so no persistence concern is set for this module itself.

A custom error class signalling that AI evaluation was aborted after repeated failures. It only builds a message and sets its name. Exception types like this are implementation details, not architectural elements. It is minor, used only by AuditAIRunner.invoke, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A nested recursive helper inside computeDirectoryHashes that walks a directory and hashes the files in it. It is a private implementation detail of the hashing utility, not an element a maintainer would name. It reads the filesystem, so data_persistence is true. The console.error call is incidental, not telemetry.

An MCP tool handler exposing the 'model_add' capability to external AI agents. It validates the layer, type and attributes, builds the element and persists it via MutationHandler or staging. This makes it a consumer-facing application service at the MCP integration boundary, and it writes the model to disk.

ValidationResult is a shared result carrier used across all validators. It holds error and warning lists and has only trivial accessors, merge and serialization helpers, so it is a passive application data object. Its wide use makes it notable, but it has no behaviour of its own.

A pluggable Exporter implementation that serializes the model to GraphML. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit used by the export command and the MCP export tool. It emits telemetry spans directly, but it only returns a string and does not write to storage itself. It is a notable format plugin rather than a core element.

An inline arrow function inside a color map that wraps a string in red ANSI colour for CLI severity output. It is a trivial formatting helper with no callers or architectural role, so it is not modelled as an element. It only touches the user interface by colouring CLI text.

Core module providing the DependencyTracker class, which performs graph-based dependency tracing and impact analysis over model elements via the reference registry. It is a cohesive, replaceable analysis component in the CLI core. It does no I/O, auth or UI work itself, only in-memory graph traversal.

CLI command module for 'dr reports' that registers the regenerate subcommand. It deletes and recreates the report files on disk via the orchestrator and prints CLI output. It is a cohesive command unit a maintainer would name when describing the CLI, but secondary to the core report orchestrator.

A trivial state-mutating method on the Changeset class. It sets the status field to 'committed' and updates the modified timestamp. This is an accessor-level implementation detail with no persistence or I/O of its own, so it is not an architectural element; the Changeset class itself would be the modelled element.

Reusable class wrapping Claude invocation for the audit AI evaluators. It adds rate limiting, timeouts and a consecutive-failure abort, and is injected into the node and relationship evaluators. It is a notable internal component and the integration point to an external AI process via invokeClaudeStreaming.

Exported MCP tool handler that implements the 'model_search' capability for external agents. It validates the layer and type filters, loads the model through a shared helper, and filters elements by query or source file. This makes it a consumer-facing application service exposed over MCP. It does not do persistence itself; loading is delegated to loadModel.

A small CLI options interface that holds the parsed flags for the audit-snapshots command (action, id, debug). It is argument plumbing for a single command, below the granularity of an architectural element, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

This module defines the Exporter plugin contract, export options and format metadata, plus shared layer colors and an XML escape helper. The Exporter interface is the access point that format-specific exporters implement, so it is a notable internal contract. It is not a top-level boundary.

Private helper that serializes a layer review result to a JSON file in the output directory. It writes durable storage, but it is an implementation detail of AIEvaluator's review flow rather than an architectural element on its own.

A utility function that recursively hashes the files in a directory. The integration manager uses it to detect changes and to install and update components. It is a notable internal behaviour of the integration module, not a component or service in its own right. It reads files from disk, so data_persistence is true.

CLI 'delete' command module: loads the model, traces dependents, prompts the user for confirmation, and removes the element via a mutation handler (likely persisting the change). It emits telemetry spans and renders CLI output. It is one named command among many in the CLI component, so it is modelled as an application function of notable internal significance.

A private method of ClaudeCodeAgent that consumes a spawned Claude Code subprocess's stdout and stderr, parses streamed events and resolves the result. This is internal subprocess-handling behaviour, so it counts as external integration. It is a minor internal unit inside the agent adapter, not an independently modelled element.

A private formatting helper that appends a markdown table of matched verify entries to a line buffer. It is called only by formatVerifyMarkdown and does no I/O or rendering itself. This is pure formatting, below the granularity of an architecture element.

Utility module providing SHA256 file and directory hashing to detect changes in installed integration files. It is a small internal helper capability that reads files from disk. It supports integration-sync logic but is not a service or component in its own right, so it rates as minor.

A types module defining the Importer contract (a plug-in port for format-specific importers) plus its options and result DTOs. The Importer interface is the access point through which import behaviour is invoked. It is a notable internal contract, not a core boundary, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

This module defines the passive data structures for the relationship audit system: coverage metrics, duplicate and gap candidates, balance assessments and graph analysis types. These are in-memory audit result records rather than domain schemas or storage, so they are best modelled as application data objects. They are notable to the audit module but not core architecture.

This is the bundled JSON Schema (draft-07) for the testing layer of the specification itself. It defines node schemas such as contextvariation and coverageexclusion, so it is a schema definition rather than a test asset. As a canonical data-model contract for one of the 13 layers it is architecturally significant. It performs no runtime cross-cutting work.

CLI command entry point for 'repair attribute-collision': loads the model, scans for damage, recovers values from changeset history, saves layers and writes the report file, and renders text/JSON output. It is a user-invoked capability offered by the CLI, a notable but niche maintenance command.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines the node schemas for the spec's security layer, covering its node types and their attributes. In this codebase it is a data-model contract that validates model elements, not security enforcement logic. It is a significant schema artifact of the specification.

A plain options interface carrying CLI flags for the export command. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, so it fits dataobject. Its significance is minor because it matters mainly within its own command file, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

Small helper that writes MCP tool errors to stderr, called only by runTool. It does logging work, so observability is true, but it is an implementation detail rather than a modelled telemetry element such as a log configuration or instrumentation scope.

A tiny internal type alias inside the OpenAPI exporter that describes the shape of a tag object being serialized. It is a helper data shape below the granularity a maintainer would name; it describes no API exposed by the system itself and has no callers or behaviour.

A tiny two-field local type (severity plus message) used inside the conformance command file to carry issue results. It is an implementation detail below the granularity a maintainer would name when explaining the system, so it is not an architectural element.

A trivial state mutator that resets an in-memory array on the FarmSyncState class. It has no callers and no callees, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself. It is an implementation detail below the architectural granularity threshold.

CopilotClient is a replaceable adapter component implementing BaseChatClient that integrates with the external GitHub Copilot CLI via subprocess spawning. It manages sessions and emits telemetry spans, making it an architecturally significant integration point. Permissions are imported from defaults, but the class does not itself decide access, so authorization is not marked.

An ordered per-layer evaluation loop that builds prompts, invokes the Claude AI runner, parses the responses and aggregates scores into reviews. It is a notable internal workflow of the node audit. It writes progress to stderr (CLI output), but the external Claude call is delegated to AuditAIRunner, so external_integration is false.

A pluggable exporter class implementing the Exporter interface. It converts the model's API layer into an OpenAPI 3.0 document and is used by the export command and the MCP export tool. It is a replaceable component within the export subsystem, not an API contract itself. It emits telemetry spans directly.

A passive TypeScript interface carrying the result of drift detection between a base snapshot and the current model. It holds state and has no behaviour, so it is a minor application data object used inside the snapshot manager module.

A CLI command entry point that runs an ordered chat-session workflow: it loads the model, initializes logging, detects and selects an AI client, then launches that external chat agent. It creates telemetry spans and logs directly and drives interactive CLI prompts and output. Persistence is delegated to the logger and Model.

Ordered delete workflow within MutationHandler. It stages the deletion when a changeset is active; otherwise it removes the element and its relationships, then persists. It writes durable state through staging and _persistChanges. This is a notable internal behaviour of the mutation component, not an exposed contract.

Exported analysis class that wraps the relationship catalog to classify relationships, compute category breakdowns and analyze transitivity for reports. It is a cohesive, replaceable unit with an injected dependency, so it fits applicationcomponent. It is a notable internal unit of the analysis module rather than a core boundary. It performs no I/O beyond delegating catalog loading.

This is a trivial one-line helper that clears an in-memory module-level model cache. Its only caller is a unit test, so it acts as test-reset scaffolding. It has no architectural behaviour of its own and touches no durable storage.

A small exported interface that holds per-category relationship statistics (count, percentage, predicates, average strength) for the relationship classifier's analysis output. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour, so it maps to an application dataobject. It is a minor unit with no callers.

Cohesive class in the audit subsystem that compares two audit reports across coverage, gaps, duplicates, balance and connectivity. It is used by the audit-diff command and the pipeline orchestrator. It is pure in-memory analysis with no I/O, so it is a notable internal component a maintainer would name, not a boundary.

A StagingAreaManager method that captures a model hash for drift detection and records it on the changeset. It is an internal behaviour unit of the staging component, named when explaining drift detection. Persistence is delegated to the storage and snapshot managers, so the method itself implements no cross-cutting concern.

Core module centralizing all element mutations (add/update/delete) across staging and base model, handling persistence atomically and emitting telemetry logs. A cohesive, replaceable unit that a maintainer would name when explaining how model changes are applied.

A tiny local type describing the shape of a parsed manifest file inside the relationship schema validator. It has no callers or callees. It is an implementation detail below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not an architectural element.

The module implements a custom OTLP span exporter that uses fetch for Bun compatibility. It defines the export destination, a timeout and the OTLP JSON protocol, which fits an APM ExporterConfig. As a telemetry integration point it POSTs spans to an external collector over HTTP.

An in-memory GraphModel method that removes an edge and keeps the source, destination and predicate indices consistent. It is a minor internal behaviour of the graph model component, below the level a maintainer would name when explaining the system. It writes no durable storage.
