A core engine class that computes projected model state by applying staged changesets to the base model. It owns a projection cache and loads changesets from on-disk staged storage. It is a cohesive, replaceable component used by the validator, staging manager and model, so it is significant to the changeset workflow.

Core module holding the in-memory RelationshipRegistry that catalogs relationship types and indexes relationships by source, layer and predicate. It is a cohesive internal component of the CLI's model core, slated for consolidation into GraphModel, and has no callers listed. It does no persistence or I/O, so it rates as a notable internal unit.

ExportManager is a registry and dispatcher for pluggable exporters. The CLI export command and the MCP export tool both use it, which makes it the central component of the export subsystem. It does no I/O itself: it validates the requested layers and delegates to an Exporter.

Private validation helper inside NodeResponseParser that type-checks and clamps fields of a single AI evaluation item. It is an implementation detail of the parser, not an element a maintainer would name in the architecture model, and it performs no cross-cutting work itself.

Module registering the 'element' CLI subcommand group (add/list/show/delete/update) with commander. It defines CLI command bindings that delegate to existing command handlers. This makes it an access point (CLI interface) rather than behaviour. It is a moderately notable alias surface, and it drives the user-facing CLI definition.

A trivial one-line helper that derives a cache key from an optional root path, used only by loadModel and reloadModel. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity. It does not itself access storage, so no cross-cutting concern applies.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of the source_reference base-node field (provenance, locations, repository). It is a domain data type in the model's own schema, best modelled as an object schema. It is notable but not central, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Bundled JSON configuration file that declares the codebase-memory-mcp analyzer: its binary, required and optional MCP tool contract, and the mappings from its graph labels to DR layers and element types. As a deployed config artifact that drives code extraction, it is architecturally significant. It is declarative data, so it performs no integration work itself.

A small in-memory statistics accessor on RelationshipRegistry. It counts relationships, unique predicates, layers and types, and has no callers. It is a helper below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A small passive TypeScript interface that carries optional error metadata: operation, context, related elements and partial progress. It lives in the errors utility and has no callers in the graph. At most a minor DataObject supporting error handling; it has no behaviour and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Manifest is a core state-carrying class for model project metadata (name, version, changeset history, external models) with constructor migration and toJSON serialization. It holds data rather than doing I/O, so it is a DataObject. It is central to the model (used by Model.init/load and many tests), so significance is high.

A small internal type holding summary counts for the validation formatter's output. It has no callers and no behaviour, and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not modelled as an element. At most it would be a minor dataobject.

Private helper that only assembles a VerifyReport object from precomputed buckets and computes summary counts. It is called solely by computeReport and is an implementation detail of the VerifyEngine component, below the granularity at which an architecture model records elements. It does no I/O or external calls.

MCP tool module exposing the model_stats capability to external MCP clients. It defines the tool contract and a handler that loads the model and delegates to StatsCollector. This is a consumer-facing offering, so applicationservice fits. It serves an external MCP protocol; persistence happens in the delegated loadModel.

Private helper that shallow-copies a Layer and its elements for projection. It is an implementation detail of VirtualProjectionEngine.projectLayer with no independent architectural role and does no I/O; marking the clone clean only prevents later saves.

Module exporting SemanticValidator, a validator class within the CLI's validation pipeline that checks relationship predicates against the spec index and flags inferred APM elements. It is a cohesive internal unit a maintainer would name, but it sits below the CLI's top-level entry points. It does no I/O itself.

A public method on SpecDataService that looks up which relationship predicates are valid between two spec node types. This is the lookup the CLI uses to validate relationship triples and suggest alternatives. It is a notable query capability inside the service, with no callers recorded and no I/O of its own (it reads already-loaded spec data).

Core service class that wraps SpecDataLoader and gives a query API over specification data: layers, node types, relationships and metadata. It is exposed through a global singleton and holds an in-memory cache. It is a cohesive, replaceable component central to spec access. The loading I/O is delegated to the loader, so this class has no persistence concern itself.

A small internal interface holding a resolved external model's name and element ID set, used only inside the composed-reference validator. It is a local helper type with no behaviour and no callers, so it falls below the granularity of an architectural element.

A small exported type definition describing repository context (git URL and commit SHA) within the source-reference data shape. It is a passive schema component with no behaviour and no callers. It is a minor part of the source-reference model, so it is best modelled as an object schema of low significance.

ImportManager is a registry and dispatcher that owns the pluggable importers (ArchiMate, OpenAPI) and routes import requests to them by format. It is the cohesive unit behind the import command, so it is an application component. It performs no I/O itself, so none of the cross-cutting concerns apply.

A private helper that increments an in-memory cache-hit counter in a map. This is an implementation detail of the projection engine's caching, not a telemetry element: it does no OTel or exported metrics work, and it sits below modelling granularity.

A one-line convenience wrapper that delegates to findRelationshipTypes with a destination filter. It is an accessor on SpecDataLoader, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architecture element. It touches no storage, I/O or UI itself.

AuditOrchestrator is a cohesive class that composes the coverage, duplicate, gap, balance and connectivity analyzers over the relationship catalog and graph. It coordinates the relationship audit and is used by PipelineOrchestrator, so it is a significant application component. The catalog load is delegated and its logging is incidental, so no cross-cutting concern applies directly.

A small exported TypeScript interface that holds analysis results (source, target, cardinality, type) inside the data-model analyzer. It is a passive data structure used internally by analysis code, not a domain schema, so it fits application dataobject. Its importance is minor and confined to this file.

An exported TypeScript interface describing the integration version manifest: CLI version, install timestamp and per-component file hashes. It is a passive state carrier with no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It is notable to the integration module, but it does not read or write storage itself.

Core audit routine that detects exact and semantic duplicate relationships in a model. It is invoked by the model audit orchestrator and works purely in memory over its inputs, with no I/O. It is a notable internal behaviour unit of the audit component, so it is an application function rather than a service.

A trivial formatting helper that wraps a string in ANSI dim styling when colours are enabled. It is an implementation detail with no callers in the graph and below the granularity of an architecture element. It only styles text and does not itself render any user interface.

A passive TypeScript interface holding the parsed representation of a spec node schema for the audit subsystem. It is a code-level data carrier with no behaviour and is not a domain entity schema, so it is an application dataobject. It is notable within the audit module.

In-memory collection class managing a model's relationships: add, delete, find and query them, with dirty tracking. It is a cohesive core-domain unit owned by Model. It does not itself write to disk (it only serializes to an array), so it is a notable internal component rather than a persistence layer.

An in-memory graph mutation method on GraphModel that removes a node, updates its indices and cascades edge removal. It is ordinary internal behaviour of the graph component, a minor unit rather than a named architectural element. No durable storage, I/O or other cross-cutting concerns are involved.

Internal TypeScript interface describing the shape of a layer distribution file's relationship schemas, as consumed by the validator. It is a passive data structure with no behaviour and has no callers, so it matters only to its own file. Minor DataObject.

A cohesive report-generation class that renders the model README markdown. It is instantiated by ModelReportOrchestrator as a replaceable unit. It produces strings only and does no file I/O itself. This makes it a notable internal component of the reports module rather than a mere helper or a UI view.

Module containing the DataModelAnalyzer class and its result interfaces. It analyzes the architecture model's data-model layer for entities, constraints, coverage and quality. This is ordinary application analysis logic, not a schema of the system itself. It is a notable internal analysis component used for reporting.
